annotations.title: List uncategorized transactions in a window

description:
List the transactions in a date window that carry no category, so a figure that depends on categorization can say exactly what is missing before it is computed.

`from` is inclusive and `to` is EXCLUSIVE — for whole months, pass the first day of the month after the last one you want.

**These rows are measured on when the movement happened (`executed_at`), not on its accounting date.** That is deliberate and it matters: the two disagree about which MONTH a transaction belongs to for a large share of real data, and many rows carry no accounting date at all. A caller listing rows on one basis while summing a figure on the other ends up with rows it counts but cannot offer to fix. Pair this with a sum measured on the same basis.

Returns each row's identity, amount, counterparty and the classifier's pending suggestion where one exists. It lists rows with NO category; a categorized row that has not yet posted to the ledger is a booking question and is not returned here.

`delivery` says how WhatsApp shows the rows, and only WhatsApp reads it: `list` (the default) sends the numbered list in the thread, `page` sends one link to the categorize page in its place. The calling skill picks it from the row count. A page read returns at most 50 rows, and its result adds `page`: the `ref` the page's message quotes, and `line_ids`, the id of each line of the page in line order (line 1 is the first id).

`exclude_transaction_ids` drops rows the user already parked in this conversation (skipped, or sent to the web picker). Pass the ids a categorization hand-back names, so the next batch moves on instead of serving them again. The rows stay uncategorized; only this read leaves them out.

`meta.truncated: true` means the page filled and more rows exist. `meta.returned` is what came back. `totals` covers the whole window, not the page: `count`, the `amounts` per currency split by sign into `sum_negative` / `count_negative` and `sum_positive` / `count_positive` exactly as `well_sum_transactions` splits them, and `unreadable_count`. Both sums are positive magnitudes. Which side is money out is a property of the FEED, not of this read: elect it from the window's `well_sum_transactions` counts before you call either side spend or income. On a feed that stores magnitudes only, every row sits in `sum_positive` and this read cannot tell money out from money in, so state the count and the amount without a direction. State the total from `totals`; when `totals` is null and the page is truncated, report the count as a floor.

**`success: false` means the window is UNKNOWN, not empty.** The read failed, so no count exists and `returned` and `truncated` are absent rather than zero. An empty `records` on a failed read is not "nothing is uncategorized" — treating it that way reports a clean list this read never produced. Say the list could not be read.

**`figure_rows` keeps only the rows a money figure reads.** A figure that sums one side of the window, such as a burn or a cost breakdown, reads no row of the other side and no row its sum excludes, so a gate on that figure must neither count nor list them. Pass the side the elected sign convention reads as money out (`amount_sign: "negative"` on a signed feed), and copy `scope`, `exclude_internal_transfers`, `exclude_own_company` and `card_spend` from the `well_sum_transactions` call that sums the figure. The read then keeps the rows of that side whose money moved and applies the sum's own transfer rules, so the rows, `count` and `amounts` are exactly the rows with no category that the figure reads. Never pass it on a feed that stores magnitudes only: there the sign says nothing about direction. Omit it where every row must carry a category whatever its side, as in a close. Pass the same `figure_rows` on every probe and read of one gate, a resumed one included.

Do not propose categories from this list. Where the classifier has a proposal it rides on the row, and the assignment surface is where a category is chosen.

When the user asks to see, list or fix these rows, call this tool directly: its card is the answer. ⚠️ **This tool draws its card on EVERY call, the empty one included.** So when nobody asked for the list and you only need to CHECK whether anything is left (the first pass of a gate, or a re-check after a repair), call `well_get_worklist_status({ worklist: "uncategorized_window", from, to })` first, with the same scope you would pass here. It draws nothing. Call this tool after it only when it answers `open: true`.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

delivery.description: WhatsApp only: `list` sends the numbered list (default), `page` sends one link to the categorize page and reads at most 50 rows. The calling skill picks it.

exclude_transaction_ids.description: Transaction ids to leave out: the rows parked in this conversation.

figure_rows.description: Keeps only the rows the money figure behind this gate reads. See the description.

amount_sign.description: The side the elected sign convention reads as money out: "negative" on a signed feed.

card_spend.description: As on the figure's `well_sum_transactions` call: `"at_purchase"` keeps the card purchases and drops the card repayments. Needs `exclude_internal_transfers: true`.

exclude_internal_transfers.description: As on the figure's `well_sum_transactions` call: drops a transfer between two owned accounts.

exclude_own_company.description: As on the figure's `well_sum_transactions` call: drops a transfer to the workspace's own company.

scope.description: The `scope` of the figure's `well_sum_transactions` call. It picks the accounts the two exclusions test; the rows stay this workspace's own.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window, YYYY-MM-DD.

to.description: EXCLUSIVE end of the window, YYYY-MM-DD.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_list_uncategorized_window

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.
